incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: PG_CONN_POOL_EXHAUSTION fired for service=redwood-production-db (severity: high) :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-8231 created and paged the on-call rotation. Escalation -> sasha (primary)

sasha (oncall): ack'd. taking it. any customer impact known?

matt (sre): seeing elevated 502/504s on the inference API. spike started ~10m ago. request latency across gateway up too.

jun (db): PG connections at 95% of max_conn on writer. lots of active idle_in_transaction + waiting queries. looks like a scheduled batch job kicked off (analytics: nightly-calc)

sasha (oncall): nice, can we throttle/kill that job quickly? who owns it?

jun (db): it's from batch-runner svc; I can cancel the run on the writer cluster. recommended immediate: cancel job, scale pgbouncer pools, set pool_mode=transaction temporarily.

matt (sre): rolling pgbouncer increase now: 
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch deployment pgbouncer --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":3}}'
```

ops-bot: pgbouncer deployment scaling triggered by matt (replicas 1 -> 3)

pagerduty-bot: sasha acknowledged the incident at 1738001240

sasha (oncall): @carla can you start a brief customer impact note? support channel getting some reports.

carla (support): on it. rounding up customers: ~12 distinct API keys showed errors, roughly 15% of production traffic affected. escalating to account execs for any high-touch customers.

jun (db): I cancelled the long-running batch on writer (PID 9823). connections dropped ~30%. but we still have many waiting queries due to prepared transactions and some idle sessions.

matt (sre): doing an emergency pgbouncer reload to flush stale client connections: 
```bash
kubectl exec -n infra deploy/pgbouncer -- pgbouncer -R /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini
```

ops-bot: pgbouncer reload succeeded (timestamp 1738001260)

sasha (oncall): nice. any immediate improvement in application errors?

matt (sre): 502s down from 18%->6% in last 2m. tailing gateway logs shows fewer "server closed connection" traces.

jun (db): writer connection_count back to 65% now. however some backend queries are slowed because of an autovacuum backlog. I recommend: 1) promote read-replica for heavy read routes, 2) temporarily disable noncritical write paths (bulk-checks), 3) set statement_timeout for the web tier to avoid long-running queries.

sasha (oncall): can we implement statement_timeout quickly on the web tier env? set to 30s?

matt (sre): applying a config toggle to the web service (feature-flagging statement_timeout=30s) now. 

ops-bot: web-config roll triggered by matt -> rollout started

matt (sre): rollout complete. statement_timeout=30s applied to all pods.

carla (support): updating customers: short-term degraded API, some retries caused 5xxs, now improving. ETA to normal: 20-40m. posting to status.redwood.ai: partial-degradation for inference API.

jun (db): still seeing leftover prepared txs from a client library bug. I can force-discard those sessions if we want a faster recovery (small risk to mid-flight work).

sasha (oncall): what's downside? data loss?
jun (db): only if that client had uncommitted writes; we've confirmed it's the analytics batch that had the bug, not customer-facing writes. risk low. recommend discard old prepared txs older than 15m.

sasha (oncall): do it.

jun (db): ran: 
```sql
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='idle in transaction' AND now() - state_change > interval '15 minutes';
```
terminated ~24 sessions. connection usage now 38%.

matt (sre): error rate back to baseline ~1.2%. latency stabilizing. good progress.

pagerduty-bot: Notification: Incident #INC-8231 escalated to matt (secondary) at 1738001295

sasha (oncall): I'll stay on until next handoff. prepping notes for postmortem: trigger = scheduled analytics job started unexpectedly during peak, failure mode = client library left prepared transactions, mitigation = cancel job + pgbouncer scale + reload + statement_timeout + kill idle txs.

carla (support): Sent customer advisory to affected tenants. Ops/SEs flagged two paying customers for one-to-one follow-up.

ops-bot: deploy-bot detected a config change to web service during incident (statement_timeout) — recorded in audit log.

sasha (oncall): handing off to matt for 09:00-17:00 shift. matt, please take post-incident triage and assign postmortem owner.

matt (sre): taking handoff. I'll open the postmortem and schedule a quick sync with jun and batch-runner owners.

pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-8231 acknowledged by matt at 1738001318, status: mitigated (monitoring ongoing)

sasha (oncall): thanks team. leaving notes in incident doc and status page. :white_check_mark:

carla (support): closing support loop for customers who confirmed recovery. leaving tickets open for follow-ups.

jun (db): leaving a temp guardrail: add check to batch-runner CI to avoid running heavy analytics during production peak hours. will open PR.

matt (sre): postmortem owner: jun. draft due EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-8231 set to resolved=false, monitoring=true, runbook_link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-conn-pool

sasha (oncall): last check: metrics look stable for 5m. handing off complete.

matt (sre): continuing monitoring for the next 30m. will update thread if anything else pops up.

carla (support): thanks all.

ops-bot: thread auto-archived after 60m of inactivity
